# About me

Silas Bambil studies statistical methods for finance, with a focus on credit-risk model updating and tail-risk measurement. He is a graduate student in Mathematics, concentrating in Statistics, at Georgia State University. He holds an MS in Quantitative Risk Analysis and Management from Georgia State University and a BSc in Actuarial Science from KNUST.

His credit-risk research examines when recent labeled data justify retaining, recalibrating, or refitting a predictive model. He compares these choices under distribution shift and measures selection regret: the predictive cost of choosing an updating policy relative to the best available candidate. He uses simulation, cross-validation, and historical mortgage data to assess how the amount of recent information affects that cost.

In extreme-loss research, he examines discrepancies between empirical losses and fitted tail models. He uses Expected Shortfall decompositions and bounded loss layers to identify where those discrepancies arise, assess their sensitivity to exceptional records, and quantify uncertainty in sparsely observed loss regions.

## Current work

::: {.work-entry}
<p class="meta">01 / Credit risk · Working manuscript, 2026</p>

### Selection regret in credit-risk model updating

He examines how the amount of recent labeled information affects the predictive cost of selecting among retention, recalibration, and full refitting, using cross-validation, simulation, and a historical Fannie Mae application.

[Research summary](research.qmd#selection-regret)
:::

::: {.work-entry}
<p class="meta">02 / Predictive modeling · Unpublished manuscript, 2026</p>

### Prediction under distribution shift

With Shudeshna Nandy, he examines calibration, discrimination, and decision thresholds in credit-risk models, comparing updating strategies through simulation and a loan-default benchmark.

[Research summary](research.qmd#distribution-shift) · [Related software](projects.qmd#shiftadapt)
:::

::: {.work-entry}
<p class="meta">03 / Extreme value theory · Unpublished manuscript, 2026</p>

### Fire-loss severity and far-tail uncertainty

An analysis of approximately 1.25 million U.S. structure-fire loss records, exploring the stability of extreme quantiles and the sensitivity of Expected Shortfall.

[Research summary](research.qmd#fire-loss) · [Analysis code ↗](https://github.com/sdbambil1/nfirs-extreme-value-analysis)
:::

::: {.work-entry}
<p class="meta">04 / Statistical computing · In development</p>

### shiftadapt

An R package for logistic model updating and intervention selection under distribution shift, with separate data for fitting, selection, and final evaluation.

[Software & projects →](projects.qmd)
:::

## Teaching

He supports College Algebra students as a Graduate Lab Assistant at Georgia State University. Previously, he taught AP Calculus, AP Precalculus, and AP Statistics at Osceola School for the Arts.

[Courses & teaching experience →](teaching.qmd)
